import Base
import Tasks.D03

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d03 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf x y hx
  have heq : f (g.mul x y) = f y := by
    calc
      f (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f x) (f y) := hf x y
      _ = h.mul h.one (f y) := congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f y)) hx
      _ = f y := h.one_mul (f y)
  exact ⟨fun hz => heq.symm.trans hz, fun hy => heq.trans hy⟩

end Submission

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf x y hx
  have heq : f (g.mul x y) = f y := by
    calc
      f (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f x) (f y) := hf x y
      _ = h.mul h.one (f y) := congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f y)) hx
      _ = f y := h.one_mul (f y)
  exact ⟨fun hz => heq.symm.trans hz, fun hy => heq.trans hy⟩
",
  "bridge": "This is a baseline proof using only the supplied foundation. Multiplicativity transports the raw product through f. The hypothesis f x = h.one changes its first factor to h.one, and h.one_mul then gives f (g.mul x y) = f y. Equality transitivity in the two directions yields the required equivalence. No candidate properties or representation bridge are needed. Packaging is not Lean verification."
}

import Base
import Tasks.D05

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d05 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf
  have hid : h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f g.one :=
    (hf g.one g.one).symm.trans (congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one))
  calc
    f g.one = h.mul h.one (f g.one) := (h.one_mul (f g.one)).symm
    _ = h.mul (h.mul (h.inv (f g.one)) (f g.one)) (f g.one) :=
      congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f g.one)) (h.inv_mul (f g.one)).symm
    _ = h.mul (h.inv (f g.one)) (h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one)) :=
      h.mul_assoc _ _ _
    _ = h.mul (h.inv (f g.one)) (f g.one) :=
      congrArg (h.mul (h.inv (f g.one))) hid
    _ = h.one := h.inv_mul (f g.one)

end Submission

import Base
import Tasks.D06

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d06 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf x
  have cancel : ∀ {A : Type} (q : Foundation.Group A) (a b c : A),
      q.mul a b = q.mul a c → b = c := by
    intro A q a b c heq
    have heq' := congrArg (fun t => q.mul (q.inv a) t) heq
    simpa only [← q.mul_assoc, q.inv_mul, q.one_mul] using heq'
  have right_inv : ∀ {A : Type} (q : Foundation.Group A) (a : A),
      q.mul a (q.inv a) = q.one := by
    intro A q a
    apply cancel q (q.inv a)
    calc
      q.mul (q.inv a) (q.mul a (q.inv a)) =
          q.mul (q.mul (q.inv a) a) (q.inv a) :=
        (q.mul_assoc (q.inv a) a (q.inv a)).symm
      _ = q.inv a := by rw [q.inv_mul, q.one_mul]
      _ = q.mul (q.inv a) q.one := (q.mul_one (q.inv a)).symm
  have hone : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply cancel h (f g.one)
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) :=

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf x
  have cancel : ∀ {A : Type} (q : Foundation.Group A) (a b c : A),
      q.mul a b = q.mul a c → b = c := by
    intro A q a b c heq
    have heq' := congrArg (fun t => q.mul (q.inv a) t) heq
    simpa only [← q.mul_assoc, q.inv_mul, q.one_mul] using heq'
  have right_inv : ∀ {A : Type} (q : Foundation.Group A) (a : A),
      q.mul a (q.inv a) = q.one := by
    intro A q a
    apply cancel q (q.inv a)
    calc
      q.mul (q.inv a) (q.mul a (q.inv a)) =
          q.mul (q.mul (q.inv a) a) (q.inv a) :=
        (q.mul_assoc (q.inv a) a (q.inv a)).symm
      _ = q.inv a := by rw [q.inv_mul, q.one_mul]
      _ = q.mul (q.inv a) q.one := (q.mul_one (q.inv a)).symm
  have hone : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply cancel h (f g.one)
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) :=
        (hf g.one g.one).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
      _ = h.mul (f g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one (f g.one)).symm
  apply cancel h (f x)
  calc
    h.mul (f x) (f (g.inv x)) = f (g.mul x (g.inv x)) :=
      (hf x (g.inv x)).symm
    _ = f g.one := congrArg f (right_inv g x)
    _ = h.one := hone
    _ = h.mul (f x) (h.inv (f x)) := (right_inv h (f x)).symm
",
  "bridge": "This is the baseline condition, with no candidate package available. The original obligation is that a multiplication-preserving function preserves inverses. From the supplied Foundation.Group laws, the term derives left cancellation by multiplying an equality on the left by the inverse, then derives each right inverse law by left cancellation. The raw multiplication hypothesis hf proves that f(g.one) is idempotent, so cancellation identifies it with h.one. Finally hf and the derived right inverse law identify h.mul (f x) (f (g.inv x)) with h.one; the codomain right inverse law gives the same product with h.inv (f x), and cancellation gives the original goal. No extra axioms, imports, or candidate properties are used. Packaging is not Lean verification."
}

import Base
import Tasks.D08

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d08 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf op hop x y z
  apply Subtype.ext
  calc
    (op (op x y) z).val = g.mul (op x y).val z.val := hop (op x y) z
    _ = g.mul (g.mul x.val y.val) z.val :=
      congrArg (fun a => g.mul a z.val) (hop x y)
    _ = g.mul x.val (g.mul y.val z.val) := g.mul_assoc x.val y.val z.val
    _ = g.mul x.val (op y z).val :=
      congrArg (fun a => g.mul x.val a) (hop y z).symm
    _ = (op x (op y z)).val := (hop x (op y z)).symm

end Submission

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf op hop x y z
  apply Subtype.ext
  calc
    (op (op x y) z).val = g.mul (op x y).val z.val := hop (op x y) z
    _ = g.mul (g.mul x.val y.val) z.val :=
      congrArg (fun a => g.mul a z.val) (hop x y)
    _ = g.mul x.val (g.mul y.val z.val) := g.mul_assoc x.val y.val z.val
    _ = g.mul x.val (op y z).val :=
      congrArg (fun a => g.mul x.val a) (hop y z).symm
    _ = (op x (op y z)).val := (hop x (op y z)).symm
",
  "bridge": "This baseline request supplies no candidate package. The proof stays in the original subtype vocabulary. Subtype.ext reduces equality of kernel elements to equality of their underlying values. The hypothesis hop identifies each occurrence of the supplied operation with the group multiplication, congrArg transports the inner identifications, and g.mul_assoc proves the underlying associativity. The kernel-membership proofs are handled by subtype extensionality; hf is unnecessary because op already has the required subtype-valued type."
}

      rw [hf x y, hx, hy]

  "bridge": "This is the baseline condition, so no candidate definitions or properties are available or used. Unpack the two range hypotheses to obtain x and y with f x = a and f y = b. No group laws beyond the raw multiplication operation are needed."
}

import Base
import Tasks.D11

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d11 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf x hx n
  induction n with
  | zero => exact hx
  | succ n ih =>
      exact (hf _ _).trans
        ((congrArg (fun z => h.mul z z) ih).trans (h.one_mul h.one))

end Submission

import Base
import Tasks.D12

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.d12 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf x y hx hy n
  have closed (a b : G) (ha : f a = h.one) (hb : f b = h.one) :
      f (g.mul a b) = h.one := by
    calc
      f (g.mul a b) = h.mul (f a) (f b) := hf a b
      _ = h.mul h.one h.one := by rw [ha, hb]
      _ = h.one := h.one_mul h.one
  induction n with
  | zero =>
      exact ⟨hx, hy⟩
  | succ n ih =>
      exact ⟨closed _ _ ih.1 ih.2, closed _ _ ih.2 ih.1⟩

end Submission

  "request_sha256": "dd246bbd28c409748d2d8a7f16b58da4037fb23c0cd11fc35e4ccc63255480b2",
  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf x y hx hy n
  have closed (a b : G) (ha : f a = h.one) (hb : f b = h.one) :
      f (g.mul a b) = h.one := by
    calc
      f (g.mul a b) = h.mul (f a) (f b) := hf a b
      _ = h.mul h.one h.one := by rw [ha, hb]
      _ = h.one := h.one_mul h.one
  induction n with
  | zero =>
      exact ⟨hx, hy⟩
  | succ n ih =>
      exact ⟨closed _ _ ih.1 ih.2, closed _ _ ih.2 ih.1⟩
",
  "bridge": "Baseline proof in the original vocabulary; no candidate package is available or used. The local closure argument transports multiplication through hf, replaces both images by h.one using the two kernel hypotheses, and applies h.one_mul. Induction on n preserves both coordinates of the recursively defined pair: the base pair uses hx and hy, and the successor uses closure in both multiplication orders. Reduction of Nat.rec, the pair projections, and the let expression gives the original conclusion. Packaging checks request integrity and response size only; Lean verification is left to the controller."
}

import Base
import Tasks.R02

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.r02 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf x y
  have cancel : ∀ (a b c : H), h.mul a b = h.mul a c → b = c := by
    intro a b c e
    calc
      b = h.mul h.one b := (h.one_mul b).symm
      _ = h.mul (h.mul (h.inv a) a) b := by rw [h.inv_mul a]
      _ = h.mul (h.inv a) (h.mul a b) := h.mul_assoc (h.inv a) a b
      _ = h.mul (h.inv a) (h.mul a c) := congrArg (h.mul (h.inv a)) e
      _ = h.mul (h.mul (h.inv a) a) c := (h.mul_assoc (h.inv a) a c).symm
      _ = h.mul h.one c := by rw [h.inv_mul a]
      _ = c := h.one_mul c
  have fone : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply cancel (f g.one) (f g.one) h.one
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) := (hf g.one g.one).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
      _ = h.mul (f g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one (f g.one)).symm
  have invImage : h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = h.one := by
    calc
      h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = f (g.mul (g.inv x) x) := (hf (g.inv x) x).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.inv_mul x)
      _ = h.one := fone
  constructor
  · intro hk
    apply cancel (f (g.inv x)) (f x) (f y)
    calc
      h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = h.one := invImage
      _ = f (g.mul (g.inv x) y) := hk.symm
      _ = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f y) := hf (g.inv x) y
  · intro hxy
    calc
      f (g.mul (g.inv x) y) = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f y) := hf (g.inv x) y
      _ = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) := congrArg (h.mul (f (g.inv x))) hxy.symm
      _ = h.one := invImage

end Submission

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf x y
  have cancel : ∀ (a b c : H), h.mul a b = h.mul a c → b = c := by
    intro a b c e
    calc
      b = h.mul h.one b := (h.one_mul b).symm
      _ = h.mul (h.mul (h.inv a) a) b := by rw [h.inv_mul a]
      _ = h.mul (h.inv a) (h.mul a b) := h.mul_assoc (h.inv a) a b
      _ = h.mul (h.inv a) (h.mul a c) := congrArg (h.mul (h.inv a)) e
      _ = h.mul (h.mul (h.inv a) a) c := (h.mul_assoc (h.inv a) a c).symm
      _ = h.mul h.one c := by rw [h.inv_mul a]
      _ = c := h.one_mul c
  have fone : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply cancel (f g.one) (f g.one) h.one
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) := (hf g.one g.one).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
      _ = h.mul (f g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one (f g.one)).symm
  have invImage : h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = h.one := by
    calc
      h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = f (g.mul (g.inv x) x) := (hf (g.inv x) x).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.inv_mul x)
      _ = h.one := fone
  constructor
  · intro hk
    apply cancel (f (g.inv x)) (f x) (f y)
    calc
      h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) = h.one := invImage
      _ = f (g.mul (g.inv x) y) := hk.symm
      _ = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f y) := hf (g.inv x) y
  · intro hxy
    calc
      f (g.mul (g.inv x) y) = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f y) := hf (g.inv x) y
      _ = h.mul (f (g.inv x)) (f x) := congrArg (h.mul (f (g.inv x))) hxy.symm
      _ = h.one := invImage

Applying cancellation to the multiplicativity equation at (one, one) proves f one = one. Multiplicativity and g.inv_mul then show that f (inv x) multiplied by f x is one. For the forward implication, the kernel hypothesis supplies the same product with f y, so cancellation gives f x = f y. The reverse implication substitutes the equality into that inverse product and returns the original kernel equality. Packaging this term does not constitute Lean verification."

  induction t with

      exact x.property
  | branch l r hl hr =>
      change f (g.mul _ _) = h.one
      rw [hf, hl, hr, h.one_mul]

import Base
import Tasks.R04

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.r04 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf xs
  induction xs with
  | nil =>
      intro z
      rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
      intro z
      change f (List.foldl g.mul (g.mul z x) xs) =
        List.foldl h.mul (h.mul (f z) (f x)) (List.map f xs)
      rw [ih (g.mul z x), hf z x]

end Submission

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf xs
  induction xs with
  | nil =>
      intro z
      rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
      intro z
      change f (List.foldl g.mul (g.mul z x) xs) =
        List.foldl h.mul (h.mul (f z) (f x)) (List.map f xs)
      rw [ih (g.mul z x), hf z x]
",
  "bridge": "This is the baseline condition, so no candidate properties are available or used. The proof proceeds directly by induction on the input list while leaving the accumulator universally quantified. The empty-list case is definitional equality. For a cons cell, unfolding foldl and map exposes the updated accumulator g.mul z x. The induction hypothesis transports the fold of the tail at that accumulator, and the supplied preservation hypothesis hf z x identifies its image with h.mul (f z) (f x). No group laws beyond the supplied preservation hypothesis are needed. Packaging this term does not verify it in Lean."
}

import Base
import Tasks.R06

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.r06 :=
by
  intro I G H g h f hf x y hx hy
  funext i
  have hxi : f x i = h.one := congrArg (fun k : I → H => k i) hx
  have hyi : f y i = h.one := congrArg (fun k : I → H => k i) hy
  change f (g.mul x y) i = h.one
  rw [hf x y i, hxi, hyi]
  exact h.one_mul h.one

end Submission

import Base
import Tasks.R07

namespace Submission
theorem solve : Tasks.r07 :=
by
  intro G H g h f hf a x hx
  have cancel : ∀ {K : Type} (k : Foundation.Group K) (u v w : K),
      k.mul u v = k.mul u w → v = w := by
    intro K k u v w he
    have hh := congrArg (fun z => k.mul (k.inv u) z) he
    simpa only [← k.mul_assoc, k.inv_mul, k.one_mul] using hh
  have right_inv (z : G) : g.mul z (g.inv z) = g.one := by
    apply cancel g (g.inv z)
    calc
      g.mul (g.inv z) (g.mul z (g.inv z)) =
          g.mul (g.mul (g.inv z) z) (g.inv z) :=
        (g.mul_assoc (g.inv z) z (g.inv z)).symm
      _ = g.mul g.one (g.inv z) :=
        congrArg (fun t => g.mul t (g.inv z)) (g.inv_mul z)
      _ = g.inv z := g.one_mul (g.inv z)
      _ = g.mul (g.inv z) g.one := (g.mul_one (g.inv z)).symm
  have f_one : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply cancel h (f g.one)
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) :=
        (hf g.one g.one).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
      _ = h.mul (f g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one (f g.one)).symm
  calc
    f (g.mul (g.mul a x) (g.inv a)) =
        h.mul (f (g.mul a x)) (f (g.inv a)) := hf (g.mul a x) (g.inv a)
    _ = h.mul (h.mul (f a) (f x)) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun t => h.mul t (f (g.inv a))) (hf a x)
    _ = h.mul (h.mul (f a) h.one) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun t => h.mul (h.mul (f a) t) (f (g.inv a))) hx
    _ = h.mul (f a) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun t => h.mul t (f (g.inv a))) (h.mul_one (f a))
    _ = f (g.mul a (g.inv a)) := (hf a (g.inv a)).symm
    _ = f g.one := congrArg f (right_inv a)
    _ = h.one := f_one

end Submission

  "proof": "by
  intro G H g h f hf a x hx
  have cancel : ∀ {K : Type} (k : Foundation.Group K) (u v w : K),
      k.mul u v = k.mul u w → v = w := by
    intro K k u v w he
    have hh := congrArg (fun z => k.mul (k.inv u) z) he
    simpa only [← k.mul_assoc, k.inv_mul, k.one_mul] using hh
  have right_inv (z : G) : g.mul z (g.inv z) = g.one := by
    apply cancel g (g.inv z)
    calc
      g.mul (g.inv z) (g.mul z (g.inv z)) =
          g.mul (g.mul (g.inv z) z) (g.inv z) :=
        (g.mul_assoc (g.inv z) z (g.inv z)).symm
      _ = g.mul g.one (g.inv z) :=
        congrArg (fun t => g.mul t (g.inv z)) (g.inv_mul z)
      _ = g.inv z := g.one_mul (g.inv z)
      _ = g.mul (g.inv z) g.one := (g.mul_one (g.inv z)).symm
  have f_one : f g.one = h.one := by
    apply cancel h (f g.one)
    calc
      h.mul (f g.one) (f g.one) = f (g.mul g.one g.one) :=
        (hf g.one g.one).symm
      _ = f g.one := congrArg f (g.one_mul g.one)
      _ = h.mul (f g.one) h.one := (h.mul_one (f g.one)).symm
  calc
    f (g.mul (g.mul a x) (g.inv a)) =
        h.mul (f (g.mul a x)) (f (g.inv a)) := hf (g.mul a x) (g.inv a)
    _ = h.mul (h.mul (f a) (f x)) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun t => h.mul t (f (g.inv a))) (hf a x)
    _ = h.mul (h.mul (f a) h.one) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun t => h.mul (h.mul (f a) t) (f (g.inv a))) hx
    _ = h.mul (f a) (f (g.inv a)) :=
      congrArg (fun t => h.mul t (f (g.inv a))) (h.mul_one (f a))
    _ = f (g.mul a (g.inv a)) := (hf a (g.inv a)).symm
    _ = f g.one := congrArg f (right_inv a)
    _ = h.one := f_one
",
  "bridge": "This is the baseline condition, so no candidate package is available or used. The proof stays in the original Group, multiplication, inverse, unit, and multiplicativity vocabulary. First, multiplying an equality on the left by an inverse yields left cancellation from associativity, inv_mul, and one_mul. In G, cancellation derives the right inverse identity. In H, cancellation applied to the multiplicative image of the unit proves that f preserves the unit. The hypothesis f x = h.one then removes x from the image of the conjugate, and multiplicativity transports the result back to f (a * inv a), which is the unit by the derived right inverse and unit preservation. No additional imports or axioms are used. Packaging is not Lean verification."
}

/- Isolated foundation: no Mathlib and no pre-existing homomorphism API. -/
namespace Foundation

structure Group (G : Type) where
  one : G
  mul : G → G → G
  inv : G → G
  one_mul : ∀ x, mul one x = x
  mul_one : ∀ x, mul x one = x
  mul_assoc : ∀ x y z, mul (mul x y) z = mul x (mul y z)
  inv_mul : ∀ x, mul (inv x) x = one

def kernelMulGoal : Prop :=
  ∀ (G H : Type) (g : Group G) (h : Group H)
    (f : G → H) (hf : ∀ x y, f (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f x) (f y))
    (x y : G), f x = h.one → f y = h.one → f (g.mul x y) = h.one

end Foundation

import Base

namespace Theory

structure Hom {G H : Type} (g : Foundation.Group G) (h : Foundation.Group H) where
  toFun : G → H
  map_mul : ∀ x y, toFun (g.mul x y) = h.mul (toFun x) (toFun y)

def kernel {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) (x : G) : Prop :=
  f.toFun x = h.one

def Kernel {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) : Type :=
  { x : G // kernel f x }

theorem kernel_mul {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    (f : Hom g h) {x y : G} (hx : kernel f x) (hy : kernel f y) :
    kernel f (g.mul x y) := by
  change f.toFun (g.mul x y) = h.one
  calc
    f.toFun (g.mul x y) = h.mul (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) := f.map_mul x y
    _ = h.mul h.one (f.toFun y) := congrArg (fun z => h.mul z (f.toFun y)) hx
    _ = h.mul h.one h.one := congrArg (fun z => h.mul h.one z) hy
    _ = h.one := h.one_mul h.one

def Kernel.mul {G H : Type} {g : Foundation.Group G} {h : Foundation.Group H}
    {f : Hom g h} (x y : Kernel f) : Kernel f :=
  ⟨g.mul x.val y.val, kernel_mul f x.property y.property⟩

end Theory

inductive Tree (A : Type) where
